content.text: of the femoral head in children ← ischemia of capital femoral epiphysis - USU unilat
· obesity · coag abnormalities (ex, Factor V Leiden)
•most prevalent 3-12y (mean 5-7y) · skeletal immaturity · low socioeconomic status
•family hx · passive smoking · low birth wt (SGA) · delayed bone age · breech delivery · glucocorticoids · SLE - genetic mutations in families w multiple affected members
•⍉RF: advanced bone age · frequent sports participation · thin habitus - obesity = RF & poorer prognosis
PATHO: disrupted blood supply to femoral head → necrosis of bone · marrow · cartilage → epiphysis fragments & flattens as necrotic bone is resorbed → spont revasc - deformity may be permanent

•MC cause of AVN of the femoral head in children - 2° causes: sickle cell dz · glucocorticoids · Gaucher dz · kidney dz · trauma (frx · dislocation) · infection (septic joint · osteomyelitis) · chemo (leukemia)
Prognosis: age @ onset = most important factor - <6y → much better outcomes
•children can remodel the femoral head but many → incongruent hip → surg - >½ sig OA by 60y
worse w activity esp @ the end of the day
•activity-related pain ⍉always relieved by rest or meds
•may have intermittent hip · thigh · knee or groin pain
•knee pain common - hip pathology referred to the knee
•may have atrophy of the thigh musc
•thigh musc spasm · anterior thigh · calf or buttock atrophy · limb-length discrepancy
•pts may lag in bone age & height
•often norm early → ↑density of femoral epiphysis → fragmentation & resorption → healing
: ↑density of the femoral epiphysis · widening of the cartilage space
MRI - test of choice for early detection
•MRI: marrow changes · nuclear bone scan (early dz): ↓perfusion to the femoral head
ddx osteoid osteoma: benign bone tumor MC in prox femur - atraumatic aching hip pain worse @ night · relieved by NSAIDs - XR: lucency w surrounding cortical thickening

ddx septic arthritis: fever · ill-appearing · severe pain w wt bearing · active & passive ROM resisted - suggestive: fever >38.3°C · refusal to bear wt · ESR >40 mm/h · CRP >2 mg/dL (>20 mg/L) · WBC >12,000/µL - dx confirmed by organism on blood or synovial fluid culture
(NWB initially) w ortho f/u (USU self-limiting w revasc w.in 2yrs)
•may advocate for protected wt bearing during early stages until reossification = complete
•pain control & restoration of hip ROM = cornerstones of acute/initial mgnt
•⍉response to conservative measures → surg - goal: prevent comps (OA · femoral head deformity)
may be indicated in some children >8yo + more advanced dz
Goals: relieve sxs · maintain ROM · keep femoral head contained in the acetabulum (casting · surg)
Abnormality in the shape &/or stability of the shape of the femoral head & acetabulum

AKA developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) - spectrum mild → severe: mild laxity & shallow acetabulum common in first wks of life (often resolve w.o intervention) → subluxable · dislocatable · subluxed · dislocated hips
MCC: ↓P of femoral head against acetabulum → shallow socket
Exam of the hip = performed during newborn assessment soon after birth & @ every well-check visit until about 9mo of age &/or the child = walking independently
•breech @ >34wk · hx of clinical instability on exam
: assessed for hip instability · asymmetry or limited abduction
w downward P to feel for dislocatability - resulting in a “click,” “clunk,” or “jerk”
& elevation to feel for reducibility - resulting in a “click,” “clunk,” or “jerk”
•(+) Ortolani = abduct hip + anteriorly directed P → hip reduces w palpable clunk
•Barlow & Ortolani useful <3mo - both become (-) as dislocation becomes fixed
(skin folds · femur length or gait) & restricted hip abduction
•Galeazzi sign: apparent femur shortening - supine w hips & knees flexed & feet flat → knee on involved side lower - older infants >3mo
•Klisic test: >3mo - useful in bilat dislocations (leg lengths appear symm) - line from ASIS to greater trochanter normally passes thru/above umbilicus · (+) = passes below
•>1y (walking age): MC findings = gait abnl (limping) · limited hip abduction
•U/S preferred <4-6mo (depends on ossification of femoral epiphysis) - for abnl exam or RF (breech · strong family hx) - images femoral head & acetabulum w stress views for joint stability
•imaging if inconclusive exam or norm exam w RF - screening U/S @ 4-6wk for those w RF
in older children - unreliable until 4mo ← radiolucency of femoral head
•>4-6mo: femoral head begins to ossify → XR more appropriate (can use @ ≥4mo)
Mild acetabular dysplasia USU resolves on its own - f/u U/S q4wk until hip appears norm
Dislocatable or dislocated hip → bracing to maintain femoral head in acetabulum (Pavlik harness or abduction splint <6mo)
Older children w untreated dislocation → may need closed or open reduction
Monitoring w routine hip radiographs until the child = skeletally mature
Hip dislocation assessment using the Barlow & Ortolani maneuvers
Autoinflammatory mono or polyarthritis in children
•formerly Still dz or systemic JRA - boys = girls
•courses: monophasic (remits & ⍉recur) · polyphasic (wks-mos b/n recurrences) · chronic (systemic dz &/or arthritis persist)
•prognosis: ~70-96% achieve inactive dz - significant minority chronic refractory dz
•macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) = life-threatening comp → persistent fever · rash · coagulopathy · ↓WBC & plt · hepatitis · markedly ↑ferritin
- MC form - USU affects young girls
•RF (+): adolescent girls · similar to adult RA
sus in children w sxs of arthritis · signs of iridocyclitis (eye redness · pain · blurred vision · photophobia · miosis) · gen adenopathy · splenomegaly · or unexplained rash or prolonged fever
•fever often presenting sx - quotidian pattern (daily spike → spontaneous return to norm) ≥2wks
•arthritis oligo- or polyarticular - any joint, MC wrists · knees · ankles - swollen & tender but USU can bear wt
•rash pink · macular · often over torso · may be pruritic - intermittent, most prominent w fever spikes - salmon on lighter skin · erythematous or hyperpigmented on darker skin
•typically <5y · rare >10y - joint pain worse in AM & improves once child starts moving - joint warm & tender to palpation
•systemic JIA: dx of exclusion (other inflam dz · malig) - ⍉specific lab tests
•Still’s labs: markedly ↑ESR & CRP · ↑WBC · marked thrombocytosis · mild anemia common · norm UA
ddx septic bacterial arthritis: fever + painful joint effusion - USU ⍉multiple joints - acutely ill · markedly ↓ROM - ⍉rash or quotidian fever
ddx transient synovitis: after viral illness - limp · ↓ROM - self-limited - ⍉fever or abnl labs
•systemic JIA: NSAIDs for acute mild-mod dz
•severe or NSAID-refractory systemic JIA → biologic DMARDs (IL inhibitors): anakinra · canakinumab · tocilizumab
•other options: glucocorticoids · MTX · intra-articular corticosteroids · TNF-α antagonists
•stem cell transplant occasionally for severe refractory dz
